title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: 5.1.2 Text Cleaning & Normalization
summary: Raw text is messy! Real-world text data contains: Inconsistent capitalization; Special characters and punctuation; HTML tags and URLs; Numbers (sometimes noise, sometimes signal); Emojis and unicode symbols; Extra whitespace
objectives: Handle special characters, URLs, and HTML tags
Understand when and why to apply each cleaning step

sections.title: Why Clean Text?
sections.body:
Raw text is messy! Real-world text data contains:
- Inconsistent capitalization
- Special characters and punctuation
- HTML tags and URLs
- Numbers (sometimes noise, sometimes signal)
- Emojis and unicode symbols
- Extra whitespace

```
Visual: Raw → Clean Pipeline

Raw Text:
"Check this out!!! 😍 Visit https://example.com for 50% OFF!! #Amazing"

After Cleaning:
"check out visit example for off amazing"
```

**Key Question**: What to keep? What to remove?
**Answer**: It depends on your task!

sections.title: 1 Lowercasing
sections.body:
### Why Lowercase?

Treating "Hello", "hello", and "HELLO" as the same word.

```
Visual Comparison:

Without Lowercasing:
┌──────────┬───────┐
│   Word   │ Count │
├──────────┼───────┤
│  Hello   │   1   │
│  hello   │   2   │
│  HELLO   │   1   │
└──────────┴───────┘
4 tokens total

With Lowercasing:
┌──────────┬───────┐
│   Word   │ Count │
├──────────┼───────┤
│  hello   │   4   │
└──────────┴───────┘
1 token type
```

### Implementation

```python
text = "Hello World! PYTHON is Amazing"

# Method 1: Built-in
lowered = text.lower()
print(lowered)  # "hello world! python is amazing"

# Method 2: Case folding (more aggressive)
casefolded = text.casefold()
print(casefolded)  # Similar to lower(), better for non-English
```

### When NOT to Lowercase

```python
# ❌ Named Entity Recognition (NER)
"Apple released iPhone"  # "Apple" = company vs "apple" = fruit

# ❌ Sentiment Analysis (sometimes)
"I LOVE this!"  # Emphasis might matter

# ❌ Code or technical text
"TypeError vs typeerror"  # Case matters in programming
```

sections.title: 2 Punctuation Handling
sections.body:
### Understanding Punctuation

```
Visual: Types of Punctuation

Sentence-ending:  . ! ?
Separators:       , ; :
Quotation:        " ' ` 
Brackets:         ( ) [ ] { }
Symbols:          @ # $ % & * + - / \ = _ | ~ ^
```

### Strategy 1: Remove All Punctuation

```python
import string

text = "Hello, World! How are you?"
print(string.punctuation)  # !"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_`{|}~

# Remove all punctuation
cleaned = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
print(cleaned)  # "Hello World How are you"
```

### Strategy 2: Keep Some Punctuation

```python
text = "I paid $50.99 for a high-quality book!"

# Keep hyphens and apostrophes
import re
# Remove all except hyphens, apostrophes, periods (for decimals)
cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w\s\-'.]", '', text)
print(cleaned)  # "I paid 50.99 for a high-quality book"
```

### Strategy 3: Replace with Spaces

```python
text = "word1,word2;word3"

# Replace punctuation with spaces
for punct in string.punctuation:
    text = text.replace(punct, ' ')
print(text)  # "word1 word2 word3"
```

### Decision Matrix

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────┬─────────────────┐
│       Task          │  Action  │     Reason      │
├─────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────────────┤
│ Sentiment Analysis  │   Keep   │ ! and ? matter  │
│ Topic Classification│  Remove  │ Usually noise   │
│ Machine Translation │   Keep   │ Structure matter│
│ Text Generation     │   Keep   │ Natural output  │
└─────────────────────┴──────────┴─────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 3 Number Handling
sections.body:
### Four Strategies

#### Strategy 1: Keep All Numbers
```python
text = "I bought 3 apples for $5.99 in 2024"
# Keep as is: "I bought 3 apples for $5.99 in 2024"
```

#### Strategy 2: Remove All Numbers
```python
import re
text = "I bought 3 apples for $5.99 in 2024"
cleaned = re.sub(r'\d+', '', text)
print(cleaned)  # "I bought  apples for $. in "
```

#### Strategy 3: Replace with Token
```python
text = "I bought 3 apples for $5.99 in 2024"
cleaned = re.sub(r'\d+\.?\d*', '<NUM>', text)
print(cleaned)  # "I bought <NUM> apples for $<NUM> in <NUM>"
```

#### Strategy 4: Spell Out (for specific cases)
```python
from num2words import num2words

text = "I have 42 apples"
# "I have forty-two apples"
```

### Visual Decision Tree

```
                    Should I keep numbers?
                           │
                ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                │                     │
           Task involves          Task focuses on
           quantities?            general meaning?
                │                     │
              Keep                  Remove or
             Numbers                Replace
                                      │
                                ┌─────┴─────┐
                              Remove      Replace
                             Entirely     with <NUM>
```

sections.title: 4 Emoji & Special Symbols
sections.body:
### Understanding Emojis

```python
text = "I love Python! 🐍 😍 🚀"

# Check emoji
def contains_emoji(text):
    import emoji
    return any(char in emoji.EMOJI_DATA for char in text)

print(contains_emoji(text))  # True
```

### Strategy 1: Remove Emojis

```python
import re

def remove_emoji(text):
    emoji_pattern = re.compile(
        "["
        u"\U0001F600-\U0001F64F"  # emoticons
        u"\U0001F300-\U0001F5FF"  # symbols & pictographs
        u"\U0001F680-\U0001F6FF"  # transport & map symbols
        u"\U0001F1E0-\U0001F1FF"  # flags
        u"\U00002702-\U000027B0"
        u"\U000024C2-\U0001F251"
        "]+", flags=re.UNICODE)
    return emoji_pattern.sub(r'', text)

text = "Great job! 👍 🎉"
print(remove_emoji(text))  # "Great job!  "
```

### Strategy 2: Convert to Text

```python
import emoji

text = "I love Python! 🐍 😍"
demojized = emoji.demojize(text)
print(demojized)  # "I love Python! :snake: :smiling_face_with_heart-eyes:"

# Or convert back
emojized = emoji.emojize(demojized)
print(emojized)  # "I love Python! 🐍 😍"
```

### Strategy 3: Extract Emoji Features

```python
def emoji_features(text):
    """Count emojis as features"""
    import emoji
    emoji_count = sum(1 for char in text if char in emoji.EMOJI_DATA)
    return emoji_count

text = "Amazing! 😍 🎉 🚀"
print(f"Emoji count: {emoji_features(text)}")  # 3
```

sections.title: 5 HTML Tags & URLs
sections.body:
### Removing HTML Tags ```python from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html_text = "

This is bold and italic text.

" # Method 1: BeautifulSoup soup = BeautifulSoup(html_text, 'html.parser') clean_text = soup.get_text() print(clean_text) # "This is bold and italic text." # Method 2: Regex (quick and dirty) import re clean_text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', html_text) print(clean_text) # "This is bold and italic text." ``` ### Removing URLs ```python import re text = "Check out https://example.com and www.test.com for more info!" def remove_urls(text): # Remove http/https URLs text = re.sub(r'http\S+', '', text) # Remove www URLs text = re.sub(r'www\.\S+', '', text) return text.strip() cleaned = remove_urls(text) print(cleaned) # "Check out and for more info!" # Or replace with token def replace_urls(text): text = re.sub(r'http\S+|www\.\S+', '', text) return text cleaned = replace_urls(text) print(cleaned) # "Check out and for more info!" ``` ### Extracting Domains (when URLs matter) ```python from urllib.parse import urlparse url = "https://www.example.com/page?query=123" domain = urlparse(url).netloc print(domain) # "www.example.com" ```

sections.title: 6 Whitespace Normalization
sections.body:
### Types of Whitespace Issues

```
Visual Problems:

1. Multiple spaces:     "hello    world"
2. Leading spaces:      "   hello"
3. Trailing spaces:     "hello   "
4. Tabs:                "hello\tworld"
5. Newlines:            "hello\nworld"
```

### Comprehensive Whitespace Cleaning

```python
import re

def normalize_whitespace(text):
    # Replace tabs and newlines with spaces
    text = text.replace('\t', ' ').replace('\n', ' ').replace('\r', ' ')
    
    # Replace multiple spaces with single space
    text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text)
    
    # Remove leading and trailing whitespace
    text = text.strip()
    
    return text

text = "  Hello   World\t\n  How   are   you?  "
cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
print(f"'{cleaned}'")  # "'Hello World How are you?'"
```

sections.title: 7 Special Characters & Accents
sections.body:
### Handling Accented Characters

```python
import unicodedata

text = "café, naïve, résumé"

# Option 1: Keep as is (recommended for most cases)
print(text)  # "café, naïve, résumé"

# Option 2: Remove accents (normalize to ASCII)
def remove_accents(text):
    # NFD = decompose characters
    nfd = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text)
    # Filter out combining marks
    return ''.join(char for char in nfd 
                   if unicodedata.category(char) != 'Mn')

cleaned = remove_accents(text)
print(cleaned)  # "cafe, naive, resume"

# Option 3: Replace with closest ASCII
from unidecode import unidecode
cleaned = unidecode(text)
print(cleaned)  # "cafe, naive, resume"
```

sections.title: Complete Cleaning Pipeline
sections.body:
### Comprehensive Text Cleaner

```python
import re
import string
import unicodedata
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

class TextCleaner:
    def __init__(self, 
                 lowercase=True,
                 remove_html=True,
                 remove_urls=True,
                 remove_emoji=True,
                 remove_punctuation=True,
                 remove_numbers=False,
                 normalize_whitespace=True):
        
        self.lowercase = lowercase
        self.remove_html = remove_html
        self.remove_urls = remove_urls
        self.remove_emoji = remove_emoji
        self.remove_punctuation = remove_punctuation
        self.remove_numbers = remove_numbers
        self.normalize_whitespace = normalize_whitespace
    
    def clean(self, text):
        """Apply all cleaning steps"""
        
        # 1. Remove HTML
        if self.remove_html:
            text = self._remove_html_tags(text)
        
        # 2. Remove URLs
        if self.remove_urls:
            text = self._remove_urls(text)
        
        # 3. Remove emojis
        if self.remove_emoji:
            text = self._remove_emoji(text)
        
        # 4. Lowercase
        if self.lowercase:
            text = text.lower()
        
        # 5. Remove numbers
        if self.remove_numbers:
            text = re.sub(r'\d+', '', text)
        
        # 6. Remove punctuation
        if self.remove_punctuation:
            text = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
        
        # 7. Normalize whitespace
        if self.normalize_whitespace:
            text = self._normalize_whitespace(text)
        
        return text
    
    def _remove_html_tags(self, text):
        soup = BeautifulSoup(text, 'html.parser')
        return soup.get_text()
    
    def _remove_urls(self, text):
        return re.sub(r'http\S+|www\.\S+', '', text)
    
    def _remove_emoji(self, text):
        emoji_pattern = re.compile(
            "["
            u"\U0001F600-\U0001F64F"
            u"\U0001F300-\U0001F5FF"
            u"\U0001F680-\U0001F6FF"
            u"\U0001F1E0-\U0001F1FF"
            u"\U00002702-\U000027B0"
            u"\U000024C2-\U0001F251"
            "]+", flags=re.UNICODE)
        return emoji_pattern.sub(r'', text)
    
    def _normalize_whitespace(self, text):
        text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text)
        return text.strip()

# Usage
cleaner = TextCleaner(
    lowercase=True,
    remove_punctuation=True,
    remove_urls=True
)

text = "Check out https://example.com! This is AMAZING 😍 #NLP"
cleaned = cleaner.clean(text)
print(cleaned)  # "check out this is amazing nlp"
```

sections.body:

sections.body:
### Example 1: Social Media Text ```python text = """ @user1 Check this out!!! 😍🔥 https://example.com/amazing-deal 50% OFF TODAY ONLY!!! #Sale #Shopping RT if you agree! 💯 """ # For sentiment analysis (keep emphasis) cleaner_sentiment = TextCleaner( lowercase=True, remove_urls=True, remove_emoji=False, # Keep for sentiment! remove_punctuation=False # Keep ! for emphasis ) print(cleaner_sentiment.clean(text)) # For topic modeling (remove noise) cleaner_topic = TextCleaner( lowercase=True, remove_urls=True, remove_emoji=True, remove_punctuation=True ) print(cleaner_topic.clean(text)) ``` ### Example 2: Customer Reviews ```python review = """
I bought this product for $49.99 and it's AMAZING!!! Highly recommend 👍👍👍 Visit my blog at www.example.com for more reviews.
""" cleaner = TextCleaner( remove_html=True, remove_urls=True, remove_emoji=True, lowercase=True ) cleaned = cleaner.clean(review) print(cleaned) # "i bought this product for 4999 and its amazing highly recommend visit my blog at for more reviews" ``` ### Example 3: News Articles ```python article = """

Breaking News: Tech Company Valued at $1.5B

The startup, founded in 2020, has grown exponentially...

Read more """ # Keep numbers and some structure for news cleaner = TextCleaner( remove_html=True, remove_urls=True, lowercase=False, # Keep for named entities remove_numbers=False, # Keep for context remove_punctuation=False # Keep sentence structure ) cleaned = cleaner.clean(article) print(cleaned) ```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
### The Cleaning Hierarchy

```
Level 1: Essential (Almost Always)
├── Normalize whitespace
├── Handle encoding properly
└── Remove HTML/XML tags

Level 2: Task-Dependent (Decide Based on Use Case)
├── Lowercasing
├── Punctuation removal
├── Number handling
└── URL handling

Level 3: Optional (Rarely Needed)
├── Accent removal
├── Emoji handling
└── Special character normalization
```

### Golden Rules

```
✓ DO:
  • Clean data consistently
  • Document your cleaning steps
  • Test on sample data first
  • Consider the downstream task
  • Preserve important information

✗ DON'T:
  • Over-clean (losing signal)
  • Under-clean (keeping noise)
  • Apply same cleaning to all tasks
  • Clean without understanding impact
  • Modify original data (keep raw copy)
```
